# Retrospective WIS Evaluation

```{r pipeline-wis}
# Reference dates to include in evaluation (matches Reich lab dashboard 2025-2026 season)
# These are the CDC submission dates for the current season
EVAL_REFERENCE_DATES <- as.Date(c('2025-11-22', '2025-11-29', '2025-12-06', '2025-12-13', '2025-12-20'))

# Helper: latest file in a directory by pattern
latest_file <- function(dir, pattern) {
  files <- list.files(dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  files[order(files)][length(files)]
}

# Load latest actuals
actual_path <- latest_file('../data/imputed_sets', '^imputed_and_stitched_hosp_\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.csv$')
stopifnot(!is.na(actual_path))
actual_raw <- read_csv(actual_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Map location_name -> FIPS
location_to_fips <- c(
  'Alabama'='01','Alaska'='02','Arizona'='04','Arkansas'='05','California'='06','Colorado'='08','Connecticut'='09','Delaware'='10',
  'District of Columbia'='11','Florida'='12','Georgia'='13','Hawaii'='15','Idaho'='16','Illinois'='17','Indiana'='18','Iowa'='19',
  'Kansas'='20','Kentucky'='21','Louisiana'='22','Maine'='23','Maryland'='24','Massachusetts'='25','Michigan'='26','Minnesota'='27',
  'Mississippi'='28','Missouri'='29','Montana'='30','Nebraska'='31','Nevada'='32','New Hampshire'='33','New Jersey'='34','New Mexico'='35',
  'New York'='36','North Carolina'='37','North Dakota'='38','Ohio'='39','Oklahoma'='40','Oregon'='41','Pennsylvania'='42','Puerto Rico'='72',
  'Rhode Island'='44','South Carolina'='45','South Dakota'='46','Tennessee'='47','Texas'='48','Utah'='49','Vermont'='50','Virginia'='51',
  'Washington'='53','West Virginia'='54','Wisconsin'='55','Wyoming'='56','US'='US'
)

actual_data <- actual_raw %>%
  transmute(location = location_to_fips[location_name], date = as.Date(date), actual_value = total_hosp) %>%
  filter(!is.na(location))

# Load model retrospective files for h=1..4
# NOTE: Local models use data cutoff date as reference_date, but CDC convention uses
# the Saturday after (reference_date + 7 days). We add 7 days to align with GitHub submissions.
# NOTE: Local files already have CDC horizon convention (0-3) in the 'horizon' column,
#       we just use that directly as 'h'.
load_model <- function(path, model_name, h_file){
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  df$model <- model_name
  df$h <- as.integer(df$horizon)  # Use horizon from file directly (already CDC convention 0-3)
  df <- df %>% mutate(
    reference_date = as.Date(reference_date),  # Already CDC convention
    target_end_date = as.Date(target_end_date)
  )
  df
}

# Load local models - file names use h=1-4, but horizon column inside already has CDC convention 0-3
all_model_dfs <- list()
for (h_file in 1:4) {
  baseline <- load_model(sprintf('../forecasts/retrospective/Flusight-baseline_h%d_forecasts.csv', h_file), 'FluSight-baseline', h_file)
  arima <- load_model(sprintf('../forecasts/retrospective/arima/ARIMA_h%d_forecasts.csv', h_file), 'ARIMA', h_file)
  lgbm_blended <- load_model(sprintf('../forecasts/retrospective/lgbm_blended/LGBM-blended_h%d_forecasts.csv', h_file), 'LGBM_blended', h_file)
  lgbm_bounded <- load_model(sprintf('../forecasts/retrospective/lgbm_enhanced_t10_bounded/TwoStage-FrozenMu_h%d_forecasts.csv', h_file), 'LGBM_bounded', h_file)
  svm <- load_model(sprintf('../forecasts/retrospective/svm_t100/svm_retrospective_h%d.csv', h_file), 'SVM', h_file)
  dfs <- list(baseline, arima, lgbm_blended, lgbm_bounded, svm)

  # Load bounded-wide variants 1-5
  for (v in 1:5) {
    lgbm_bounded_wide_v <- load_model(
      sprintf('../forecasts/retrospective/lgbm_enhanced_t10_bounded_wide_%d/TwoStage-FrozenMu_h%d_forecasts.csv', v, h_file),
      sprintf('LGBM_bounded_wide_%d', v), h_file)
    if (!is.null(lgbm_bounded_wide_v)) {
      dfs <- c(dfs, list(lgbm_bounded_wide_v))
    }
  }

  dfs <- dfs[!sapply(dfs, is.null)]
  if (length(dfs) > 0) all_model_dfs[[h_file]] <- bind_rows(dfs)
}
# Combine all local models into one dataframe (h column already has correct CDC convention)
all_local_models <- bind_rows(all_model_dfs)

# Load AdaptiveEnsemble and FluSight-baseline from CDC GitHub
# This ensures we're scoring the actual submitted forecasts and using the official baseline
# Models use CDC horizon convention (0-3), we need to convert to internal (1-4)
github_base_url <- 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub/main/model-output'

# 2025-26 season CDC dates available on GitHub
github_dates <- c('2025-11-22', '2025-11-29', '2025-12-06', '2025-12-13', '2025-12-20')

# Helper function to load model from GitHub
load_github_model <- function(model_dir, model_name, internal_name, dates) {
  model_list <- list()
  for (cdc_date in dates) {
    url <- sprintf('%s/%s/%s-%s.csv', github_base_url, model_dir, cdc_date, model_name)

    tryCatch({
      df <- read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE)
      df <- df %>%
        filter(output_type == 'quantile',
               horizon >= 0,  # Exclude negative horizons
               target == 'wk inc flu hosp') %>%  # Only hospitalization target, not ED visits
        mutate(
          model = internal_name,
          h = as.integer(horizon),  # Keep CDC horizon convention (0-3)
          reference_date = as.Date(reference_date),
          target_end_date = as.Date(target_end_date),
          output_type_id = as.numeric(output_type_id),  # Ensure numeric for binding
          location = sprintf('%02s', location)  # Ensure 2-char format for location
        )
      model_list[[cdc_date]] <- df
    }, error = function(e) {
      message(sprintf("Could not fetch %s from GitHub for %s: %s", model_name, cdc_date, e$message))
    })
  }
  if (length(model_list) > 0) bind_rows(model_list) else NULL
}

# Load AdaptiveEnsemble (MIGHTE-Nsemble) from GitHub
ensemble_all <- load_github_model('MIGHTE-Nsemble', 'MIGHTE-Nsemble', 'AdaptiveEnsemble', github_dates)

# Load FluSight-baseline from GitHub (official baseline for relative WIS calculation)
baseline_github <- load_github_model('FluSight-baseline', 'FluSight-baseline', 'FluSight-baseline', github_dates)

# Combine all models: start with local models, replace local baseline with GitHub version,
# and add AdaptiveEnsemble from GitHub
ret_all <- all_local_models

# Replace local baseline with GitHub baseline if available
if (!is.null(baseline_github)) {
  ret_all <- ret_all %>% filter(model != 'FluSight-baseline')
  ret_all <- bind_rows(ret_all, baseline_github)
}

# Add AdaptiveEnsemble from GitHub
if (!is.null(ensemble_all)) {
  ret_all <- bind_rows(ret_all, ensemble_all)
}

# Deduplicate: For each (model, h, location, target_end_date), keep only the row from
# the correct reference_date. The correct reference_date for a given (h, target_end_date)
# is target_end_date - (h * 7 days). This matches how the Reich lab evaluates forecasts.
ret_all <- ret_all %>%
  mutate(expected_ref_date = as.Date(target_end_date) - (h * 7)) %>%
  filter(as.Date(reference_date) == expected_ref_date) %>%
  select(-expected_ref_date)

stopifnot(nrow(ret_all) > 0)

# Use scoringutils::wis for WIS calculation (matches hubEvals/Reich lab dashboard)
calculate_wis_single <- function(qvals, qlevels, actual_value){
  if (length(actual_value) == 0 || all(is.na(actual_value))) return(NA_real_)
  qv <- as.numeric(qvals)
  ql <- as.numeric(qlevels)
  y <- as.numeric(actual_value)[1]
  if (!is.finite(y)) return(NA_real_)
  keep <- is.finite(qv) & is.finite(ql)
  qv <- qv[keep]; ql <- ql[keep]
  if (length(qv) == 0 || length(ql) == 0) return(NA_real_)

  # Sort by quantile level
  ord <- order(ql)
  qv <- qv[ord]
  ql <- ql[ord]

  # Use scoringutils::wis directly
  tryCatch({
    scoringutils::wis(
      observed = y,
      predicted = qv,
      quantile_level = ql,
      weigh = TRUE,
      count_median_twice = FALSE
    )
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

# Compute WIS - filter by reference date (same dates for all horizons, matching Reich lab)
wis_scores_all <- list()
for (h in sort(unique(ret_all$h))) {
  dfh <- ret_all %>%
    filter(h == !!h, output_type == 'quantile', as.Date(reference_date) %in% EVAL_REFERENCE_DATES) %>%
    mutate(output_type_id = as.numeric(output_type_id))
  if (nrow(dfh) == 0) next

  grouped <- dfh %>%
    group_by(h, model, reference_date, target_end_date, location) %>%
    summarise(quantile_values = list(value), quantile_levels = list(output_type_id), .groups = 'drop')

  with_actual <- grouped %>%
    left_join(actual_data, by = c('target_end_date' = 'date', 'location' = 'location'))

  wis_scores <- with_actual %>%
    filter(!is.na(actual_value)) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(interval_score = calculate_wis_single(unlist(quantile_values), unlist(quantile_levels), actual_value)) %>%
    ungroup()

  wis_scores_all[[paste0('h', h)]] <- wis_scores
}

# Exclude only US national for state-level evaluation (Reich lab dashboard includes Puerto Rico)
wis_scores_all_df <- bind_rows(wis_scores_all) %>% filter(location != 'US')

# For relative WIS calculation, we need common (location, target_end_date, h) units
# between each model and the baseline (FluSight-baseline)
# This matches Reich lab dashboard which scores each model based on overlap with baseline

# Get baseline coverage
baseline_coverage <- wis_scores_all_df %>%
  filter(model == 'FluSight-baseline') %>%
  select(h, location, target_end_date, reference_date)

# For each model, find common units with baseline
wis_scores_common <- wis_scores_all_df %>%
  semi_join(baseline_coverage, by = c('h', 'location', 'target_end_date'))

# Pairwise relative WIS calculation (matches scoringutils/Reich lab dashboard methodology)
# For each (location, target_end_date) unit, compute ratio of each model's WIS to baseline's WIS
# Then take geometric mean across all units for each model

compute_pairwise_relative_wis <- function(df, baseline_model = 'FluSight-baseline') {
  # Ensure h is integer for proper joining
  df <- df %>% mutate(h = as.integer(h))

  # Get baseline WIS for each unit
  baseline_wis <- df %>%
    filter(model == baseline_model) %>%
    select(h, location, target_end_date, baseline_wis = interval_score)

  # Join and compute ratio for each model's forecast unit
  df_with_ratio <- df %>%
    left_join(baseline_wis, by = c('h', 'location', 'target_end_date')) %>%
    filter(!is.na(baseline_wis), baseline_wis > 0) %>%
    mutate(wis_ratio = interval_score / baseline_wis)

  # Geometric mean of ratios per model (this is the "theta" in scoringutils)
  df_with_ratio %>%
    group_by(h, model) %>%
    summarise(
      relative_wis = exp(mean(log(wis_ratio), na.rm = TRUE)),
      geometric_mean_wis = exp(mean(log(interval_score), na.rm = TRUE)),
      n_units = n(),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
}

per_horizon_summary <- compute_pairwise_relative_wis(wis_scores_common) %>%
  arrange(h, is.na(relative_wis), relative_wis)

# Combined across horizons - only include models with all available horizons
n_horizons_with_data <- n_distinct(wis_scores_common$h)

models_with_all_horizons <- wis_scores_common %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(n_horizons = n_distinct(h), .groups='drop') %>%
  filter(n_horizons == n_horizons_with_data) %>%
  pull(model)

# For combined, compute pairwise relative WIS across all horizons together
wis_common_all_h <- wis_scores_common %>%
  filter(model %in% models_with_all_horizons)

# Get baseline WIS for each unit (ignoring horizon for combined calculation)
baseline_wis_combined <- wis_common_all_h %>%
  filter(model == 'FluSight-baseline') %>%
  select(location, target_end_date, h, baseline_wis = interval_score)

combined_with_ratio <- wis_common_all_h %>%
  left_join(baseline_wis_combined, by = c('location', 'target_end_date', 'h')) %>%
  filter(!is.na(baseline_wis), baseline_wis > 0) %>%
  mutate(wis_ratio = interval_score / baseline_wis)

combined_summary <- combined_with_ratio %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    relative_wis = exp(mean(log(wis_ratio), na.rm = TRUE)),
    geometric_mean_wis = exp(mean(log(interval_score), na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_units = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(is.na(relative_wis), relative_wis)
```

## Per-Horizon Results

```{r per-horizon-table}
knitr::kable(per_horizon_summary, digits = 4, caption = "Per-Horizon Geometric Mean WIS and Relative WIS (Pairwise method)")
```

## Combined Results

Pairwise method: For each (location, date, horizon) unit, compute ratio of model WIS to FluSight-baseline WIS. Relative WIS = geometric mean of these ratios across all units.

```{r combined-table}
knitr::kable(combined_summary, digits = 4, caption = sprintf("Combined Geometric Mean WIS and Relative WIS (Horizons 0-%d)", n_horizons_with_data - 1))
```
